title: UAE Logistics Brief
lede: Iran has widened the sea war to Oman's shipping navigation systems, and another tanker was hit near Hormuz on Wednesday. On land and in the air, Saudi cargo is still the bottleneck: Emirates SkyCargo is off Riyadh and Dammam until 27 November and trucks cannot get into Riyadh.

gauges.note: Back above $90 after Tuesday's dip; up 0.2% on the day (Euronews, 11 Nov)

stories.headline: Iran attacks ship navigation systems on Oman's Didamar island
body: Three sources told Reuters that Iran attacked ship navigation systems on the Omani island of Didamar. Iranian state media said the IRGC destroyed "enemy navigation systems" there on Tuesday. Reuters could not confirm if anything was destroyed, and shipping sources expect limited impact on commercial traffic.
Gulf oil exports were back above 80% of pre-war levels in September and October. Exporters use ship-to-ship transfers off Oman and the UAE, with VLCCs shuttling to points near Sohar and Fujairah.
stories.soWhat: New: Iran is now hitting shore-side navigation in Oman, near the Sohar and Fujairah transfer zones we use as Hormuz bypasses. Keep sea war-risk charges in place.

stories.headline: Another tanker hit in Hormuz on Wednesday
body: UKMTO said on Wednesday it had a report from military authorities of an incident with a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz. Crew status, damage and environmental impact were unknown. Iran's navy said an oil tanker caught fire after hitting a naval mine in a "restricted area" east of the strait.
Separately, India said a Liberia-flagged tanker with Indian crew was hit by a projectile in the Gulf. Four crew were injured and the other 18 are safe.
stories.soWhat: New: a fourth tanker strike in three days, after yesterday's ADNOC Logistics hit. There is no sign of the sea risk easing this month.

stories.headline: Saudi cargo: SkyCargo off Riyadh and Dammam until 27 November, no trucking into Riyadh
body: Expeditors says Emirates SkyCargo has suspended Riyadh and Dammam through 27 November and runs limited Jeddah service. Emirates is trucking backlog cargo from Dubai World Central to Jeddah and Dammam, but trucking into Riyadh is not available for Emirates or Qatar Airways cargo.

Riyadh airport customs clearance is suspended and some cargo is rerouted through Jeddah. Jeddah port is open but congested, with landside delays of about 10–12 days after discharge. Cargo backlogs are building for Saudi-bound shipments.
stories.soWhat: New: the cargo side is off until 27 November, longer than passenger schedules suggest. Customers with Riyadh freight need a ground route through Dammam or Jeddah, priced for the delay.

stories.headline: MESA air volumes up 10% in October; Gulf capacity still 18% below pre-war
body: WorldACD data show Middle East and South Asia air cargo volumes rose 10% on the year in October. Arabian Gulf capacity rose 2% in week 44 but is still 18% below pre-war levels.
MESA full-market rates were up 2% on the month and 60% on the year. Global spot rates averaged $3.67/kg in October, up 37%.
stories.soWhat: Demand is up and capacity is short, so air buy rates stay high into peak. Keep air rates passed through and do not promise year-end cuts.

stories.headline: Brent back above $90 as more Gulf oil flows
body: Brent rose 0.2% to $91.71 on Wednesday morning, after dipping below $90 on Tuesday. Iran's mine claim and the US naval blockade of Iranian ports keep the market watching Hormuz.
On Monday Brent fell almost 5% to about $93.75. A Reuters survey showed OPEC output up 1.38 million barrels a day in October, to 22.87 million.
stories.soWhat: New: oil bounced back. Base any December fuel surcharge cut on an average over several weeks, not one day's price.

competitors.name: DHL
competitors.headline: Moves freight forwarding east, near Khor Fakkan and Fujairah
body: DHL Global Forwarding will strengthen its presence in the east of the UAE, near Khor Fakkan, Dibba and Fujairah, as ports there expand to bypass Hormuz. Its €500 million ($557.5 million) Gulf commitment is unchanged. It has a 20-year joint venture with Etihad Rail for the UAE freight network. MEA CEO Tobias Maier expects the industry to take three to six months to normalise after the conflict ends.
competitors.soWhat: DHL is building east-coast plus rail as its Hormuz bypass. We need our own Khor Fakkan/Fujairah offer before key accounts sign with them.

competitors.name: Iron Mountain
competitors.headline: Opens first UAE warehouse, 37,000 sqm for Unilever at Dubai South
body: Iron Mountain opened its first UAE warehousing and logistics site at EZDubai Logistics Hub in Dubai South. It consolidates Unilever's warehousing and fulfilment, with bonded and non-bonded storage, co-packing and set assembly. The site uses drones and robotic inventory counting.
competitors.soWhat: A new 3PL has won a top FMCG account in Dubai. Contract logistics must defend renewals with automation and value-added services, not just space.

competitors.name: Aramex (baseline)
competitors.headline: CEO: freight rates may take 6–12 months to ease after peace
body: Group CEO Amadou Diallo said freight rates should normalise six to 12 months after peace returns. Q2 revenue was Dh1.83 billion, up 22% and a record; first-half revenue was Dh3.43 billion, up 12%. Aramex aims for double-digit growth in 2026 and 2027, using multimodal routes via Turkish ports, Sohar, Salalah and Jeddah.
competitors.soWhat: Our public line is that high rates last well past any ceasefire. Pricing should keep contracts consistent with it.

opportunities.title: Saudi ground bridge
opportunities.text: SkyCargo is off Riyadh and Dammam to 27 November and airlines cannot truck into Riyadh. Sell UAE–Riyadh road freight with clearance via Dammam or Jeddah.

opportunities.title: East-coast bypass bundle
opportunities.text: DHL is moving to Khor Fakkan and Fujairah. Package east-coast port handling, rail and trucking into Dubai before customers commit to them.

opportunities.title: Peak air demand
opportunities.text: MESA volumes are up 10% on the year. Shippers short of Gulf capacity will pay for guaranteed uplift.

opportunities.title: FMCG contract logistics
opportunities.text: Unilever outsourced to a new 3PL in Dubai South. Other FMCG firms may be reviewing their warehouses; get on their tender lists.

watchouts.title: Attacks spread to Oman
watchouts.text: Navigation systems on Didamar were hit. Sohar and Fujairah transfer zones are close by.

watchouts.title: Jeddah congestion
watchouts.text: Landside delays of about 10–12 days. Rerouted Saudi cargo can get stuck there.

watchouts.title: New contract-logistics rivals
watchouts.text: Iron Mountain and DHL are adding UAE space and automation. Expect price pressure on renewals.

watchouts.title: Oil whipsaw
watchouts.text: Brent dipped below $90 and bounced to $91.71 in a day. A fast surcharge cut could be wrong a week later.

moves.title: Quote Riyadh freight by road via Dammam
moves.text: Air is off to 27 November and Riyadh customs is suspended. Publish a road rate and transit time for Riyadh-bound cargo today.

moves.title: Hold Gulf sea war-risk charges
moves.text: Four tanker strikes in three days plus the Didamar attack. Keep the surcharge and brief key accounts with these facts.

moves.title: Build an east-coast bypass offer
moves.text: Answer DHL's move with a Khor Fakkan/Fujairah port, rail and truck package for key importers.

moves.title: Use a multi-week average for fuel
moves.text: Set the December fuel rule on a 3–4 week Brent average so one day's swing does not trigger a cut.

moves.title: Secure peak air allocation
moves.text: Gulf capacity is still 18% short. Lock block space for December rather than waiting on spot.

moves.title: Defend FMCG warehouse renewals
moves.text: List FMCG contracts up in the next 12 months and add automation and co-packing to each renewal offer.
